sentences.text: Navajodactylus is an extinct genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur known from the Late Cretaceous of the San Juan Basin in New Mexico.
The generic name honors the Navajo Nation by combining their name with the Greek word for finger.
Researchers debate whether Navajodactylus is truly an azhdarchid because it lacks the extensive air pockets in its forelimb bones typical of that family.
Oceanographer Arjan C. Boeré discovered and collected the holotype specimen, the specimen the species is based on, from the Kirtland Formation in 2002.
Robert M. Sullivan and Denver W. Fowler named the genus Navajodactylus in 2011, with Navajodactylus boerei as the type species.
The holotype specimen dates to the upper Campanian stage, approximately 75 million years ago.
A paratype specimen consists of an ulna fragment.
Navajodactylus was tentatively placed in the family Azhdarchidae based on its age, but it lacks defining shared characteristics of that group.
Navajodactylus lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
